title: She Was Srivalli for 500 Million Fans — Now Rashmika Mandanna Is Playing the Monster
excerpt: The Pushpa pair reunites in Atlee's sci-fi fantasy Raaka, with Rashmika in her first-ever villain role, Deepika Padukone co-starring, and Hollywood VFX houses building a creature feature that could redefine Indian blockbuster cinema.
body:
There's a moment in every star's career when they get tired of being loved.

<youtube></youtube>

**Rashmika Mandanna** has reached that moment. And she's chosen the most spectacular way imaginable to announce it.

According to a fresh report from Variety India, the actress who made an entire subcontinent learn the word *Srivalli* is about to join **Allu Arjun** on the Mumbai schedule of **Raaka** — director **Atlee's** wildly ambitious sci-fi fantasy action film that has been whispered about in trade circles for months. The reunion of the *Pushpa* franchise's most beloved pair would be enough to trend for a week. But here's the twist that nobody saw coming: Rashmika is playing the villain.


![Variety India — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/5/5a/Variety_cover.jpg)


Let that sink in. The woman who danced barefoot in a red saree and launched a thousand reels is now being cast as the antagonist in what might be the most expensive Indian film ever greenlit.

## A Cast That Reads Like a Red Carpet



> **"Sources close to the production have described the role as "darker" and "a facet audiences haven't imagined for her." If it works, it elevates Rashmika from crowd-favourite to serious dramatic force."**


Raaka's ensemble is the kind of thing producers dream about and accountants have nightmares over. **Deepika Padukone** holds a key role. **Janhvi Kapoor** and **Mrunal Thakur** are reportedly part of the lineup. And at the centre of it all stands Allu Arjun, fresh off the seismic, record-smashing *Pushpa 2: The Rule*, in what the first-look poster suggests is a "were-beast" transformation role — think fur, tusks, and primal rage rendered at a level Indian cinema has never attempted.

The poster itself — unveiled on Allu Arjun's 44th birthday — showed the star with most of his face buried under thick fur, a tusk-like element jutting out with feral menace. The makers captioned it with deliberate understatement: *"Prepare yourself for a vision beyond limits."* They weren't exaggerating.


![Allu Arjun — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/09/Allu_Arjun_at_Pushpa_2_The_Rule_meet.jpg)


## Hollywood Muscle, Indian Soul

What separates Raaka from every other "big-budget Indian film" announcement is the VFX firepower behind it. The production has roped in **Legacy Effects**, **Fractured FX**, **Spectral Motion**, **Lola VFX**, and — most tellingly — **Industrial Light & Magic (ILM)**, the George Lucas-founded studio that built the dinosaurs in *Jurassic Park* and the creatures of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. These aren't names you casually attach to a project. They're names you bring in when you're building an entire world from scratch.

Reports suggest the film blends sci-fi with mythological undertones, potentially exploring different timelines or dimensions. Allu Arjun may appear in multiple avatars, each requiring extensive prosthetics and digital augmentation. For Atlee — whose last directorial, *Jawan* with Shah Rukh Khan, grossed over ₹1,100 crore worldwide — the ambition is clearly to out-scale everything he's done before.

## Rashmika's Gamble


![Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg)


The villain turn is the real headline here. Rashmika has spent the last four years building a persona that is warm, accessible, and universally adored. *Pushpa*, *Animal*, *Chhaava* — in each, she played variations of a woman defined by love, loyalty, or quiet strength. Walking into Raaka as the antagonist isn't just a casting choice. It's a career recalibration.


Details of her character remain under wraps, but the departure is clearly intentional. Sources close to the production have described the role as "darker" and "a facet audiences haven't imagined for her." If it works, it elevates Rashmika from crowd-favourite to serious dramatic force. If it doesn't — well, nobody remembers timid career decisions either.

## What NRIs Should Know

Raaka is being mounted as a pan-India, multilingual release — Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, and more — with a theatrical window planned for late 2027. Given Atlee's track record and the Allu Arjun–Rashmika reunion factor, expect it to open wide across the US, UK, Canada, and the Middle East. This is the kind of film that fills IMAX screens in Edison, Fremont, and Harrow on opening Thursday.

The Mumbai schedule is expected to kick off soon, with the production ramping up through the second half of 2026. For a film that's still deep in production, Raaka is already generating the kind of heat that most finished films would envy.

Srivalli walked so Raaka's monster could run.
